# CLAUDE.md — dist/ (host deployment package)

Guidance for Claude working on a deployment host. This directory is a
self-contained, GPU-free (CPU-only) distribution of the analyst-assist
llama.cpp server + web UI, cut from the dev repo at the parent of this file.
It targets x86_64 RedHat-compatible Linux (RHEL / Rocky / Alma / Fedora) and
must work without CUDA, Python tooling, or node.

## What is shipped vs. created

Only these files are part of the package:

    Makefile             fetch pinned llama.cpp, build CPU-only, install
    serve.sh             start script (env overrides, see below)
    webapp/index.html    the entire web application (vanilla JS, no build)
    webapp/ocmdefs.txt   the OCM codebook — verbatim copy of the dev repo's
                         data/ethnographic/ocmdefs.txt (re-copy it there if
                         the codebook changes; never edit this copy)
    webapp/samples.js    the 10 gold feedback sections, GENERATED by the dev
                         repo's `scripts/make_samples.py` (deterministic
                         seed-0 pick matching scripts/section_demo.py) —
                         regenerate there, never edit by hand. Brief eHRAF
                         excerpts the project has cleared as fair use, so
                         they may ship publicly; the full corpus still may
                         not
    README.md            user-facing instructions

Everything else is created on the host: `llama.cpp/` (fetched source, pinned
to `LLAMA_REF` in the Makefile — the commit the models were validated
against), `runtime/` (installed binaries), `models/` (drop-in .gguf). Never
commit or edit generated `llama.cpp/` source; model behavior changes belong
upstream in the dev repo.

## Install & run

    sudo dnf install -y gcc gcc-c++ make cmake git
    make                                   # fetch + build + install to runtime/
    cp /path/to/model-q8_0.gguf models/    # whichever single .gguf is served
    ./serve.sh                             # http://127.0.0.1:8080

serve.sh env overrides: `PORT` (8080), `HOST` (127.0.0.1; 0.0.0.0 exposes to
the network), `THREADS` (nproc; ~10 is plenty for the 362M model), `CTX`
(8192 — models are validated up to 8192), `MODEL` (gguf path). THREADS must
always be ≥ 1 — never `-t -1` (thread oversubscription collapses throughput).

No restart or rebuild is needed after editing `webapp/index.html` —
llama-server serves `--path webapp` from disk on every request. Edit, hard
refresh the browser.

## Web app architecture

`webapp/` is deliberately dependency-free: `index.html` is one vanilla-JS
file with no build step, plus the static `ocmdefs.txt` codebook it fetches.
Do not introduce a bundler, framework, or new JS files. Debug it with the
browser dev tools console (there is no linter or test suite here).

The UI POSTs to llama.cpp's native `/completion` endpoint (NOT
OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`). One request = one synchronous
completion:

    curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"prompt":"…","n_predict":64,"temperature":0,"stop":["\n\n"],"ignore_eos":true}'

Note: in responses, the `<|ocm|>` / `<|sec|>` special tokens do not appear in
`content` — the tag line arrives as `131 LOCATION 133 TOPOGRAPHY …`. That is
why `filterTags()` accepts the first line *starting with a digit*.

### Prompt contract (must match model training)

Single (paragraph) mode — prompt is the raw pasted text; the model continues
with the OCM tag line.

Section mode — per-paragraph prompt, matching the sec-loo eval flow:

    <|sec|>{section title}\n
    <|ocm|>{union of codes seen so far, "CODE NAME" pairs}\n
    \n
    {paragraph}\n

The union is *carried forward*: after each paragraph, codes parsed from the
model's own answer (not gold) are accumulated and fed into the next prompt.
`unionString()` orders codes by (length, lexicographic) — keep that order, it
matches training/eval. `parseCodes()` splits the answer line into
`[code, name]` pairs.

### The retry ladder (tagOnce)

1. Normal request with `stop: ["\n\n"]` (early stop at first blank line).
2. If `filterTags` finds nothing → retry with `stop: []` (a blank line
   preceded the tag line and the early stop cut it off).
3. If still nothing and temperature was 0 (Fixed) → one resample at 0.7,
   reported via `fellBack` so the status line can disclose it.

Preserve this ladder and its status-line messages when editing — it exists
because greedy decode dead-ends occasionally and the early stop is lossy.

## Editing notes

- Tag lines are rendered by `linkifyTags()`: every digit run becomes a link
  that opens `showOcm(code)` — a NON-MODAL in-page `<dialog>` (NOT
  window.open, so it works inside sandboxed iframes) pinned to the top of
  the viewport and rewritten per click; vertically resizable (`resize:
  vertical`). Every content change re-sizes the panel to its content
  height capped at the output div's top (max-height applied → height: auto
  → measure → pin → free the clamp), so a manual drag persists only until
  the next code click. The page stays interactive, and Esc
  needs the manual keydown handler (non-modal dialogs get no native
  Esc-close). Longest codebook entry ≈ 2,136 chars (code 550), so tall
  definitions scroll internally once clamped. Codes inside the dialog
  content (Summary, Related Terms) are links too — `linkifyTags(text,
  true)` only activates digit runs that are real codebook entries, so
  years/counts in prose stay inert. Shows the codebook entry
  (name, Summary, Related Terms),
  Georgia/serif at #out's font size. STASHED ALTERNATIVE: a standalone
  popup window was tried first — `window.open("", "ocm",
  "popup,width=540,height=660,…")` on a single named window, rewritten via
  `document.open()` per click (see git history of this file) — rejected for
  iframe/sandbox/mobile fragility, but preferable if detachable, comparable
  definitions are ever wanted.
  The output div therefore holds DOM
  nodes, not
  text: build results with `textContent`/`replaceChildren`, never
  `innerHTML` (model output is untrusted). "raw output" mode stays plain
  text on purpose.
- `ocmdefs.txt` is fetched at page load and parsed into the `OCM` map (code
  → name/summary/related). Codes are looked up verbatim, then zero-padded
  to 3 digits; codes missing from the codebook show "not in codebook".
- The Sample menu (`SAMPLES` from samples.js) inserts its selection into the
  input: whole section (section-title line + blank-line-separated
  paragraphs) when section mode is on, else one paragraph with a numbered
  Paragraph select. Toggling section mode re-inserts the current sample —
  keep that coupling if you touch either handler.
- `letters(i)` renders results as `a) b) … z) aa)` — zero-based, bijective
  base-26. Section mode ends with a visible blank line (an nbsp-filled
  spacer div — an empty div collapses to 0 height), then the aggregate union
  of every code seen (`unionString(seen, counts)`, linkified) where codes
  appearing in 2 paragraphs get a `+` suffix attached to the label and 3+
  get `++` — the prompt-carried union (`unionString(seen)`) stays
  unannotated. Keep output
  format
  stable; downstream users parse it.
- `ignore_eos: true` is set on all requests so `stop` sequences are the only
  terminator; if you remove it, generations may end early on the model's EOS.
- Default `n_predict` 256 is sized for the tag line + small overrun; large
  values just waste CPU decode time (early stop bounds it anyway).
- The `#status` span is the only progress/error surface — always update it
  before/after awaits and in catch blocks.
- Keep `<title>`/`<h1>` in sync if the product name changes.
